description:
Same kind of constant has two names depending on which crate defines it:

| Crate | Pattern |
|---|---|
| jmap-mail-server | JMAP_MAIL_URI, JMAP_SUBMISSION_URI, JMAP_VACATION_RESPONSE_URI |
| jmap-mail-types | JMAP_MDN_URI, JMAP_SIEVE_SCRIPTS_URI |
| jmap-{tasks,calendars,contacts,sharing,filenode}-types | JMAP_TASKS_URI, etc. |
| jmap-tasks-server | CAPABILITY_TASKS (duplicates JMAP_TASKS_URI string) |
| jmap-calendars-server | CAPABILITY_CALENDARS (duplicates JMAP_CALENDARS_URI) |
| jmap-contacts-server | CAPABILITY_CONTACTS (duplicates JMAP_CONTACTS_URI) |
| jmap-sharing-server | CAPABILITY_PRINCIPALS, CAPABILITY_PRINCIPALS_OWNER |
| jmap-filenode-server | (correctly) re-exports JMAP_FILENODE_URI from filenode-types |

Four of the seven extension servers redefine the URI string locally as CAPABILITY_*, even though the corresponding JMAP_*_URI exists in their types crate. Two issues:

1. Naming inconsistency: CAPABILITY_X vs JMAP_X_URI for the same kind of value
2. Duplication: if the URI changes upstream (e.g. RFC publication renames a draft), the server crate's constant goes stale

Fix: define each URI exactly once in the types crate as JMAP_<X>_URI. Have the server crate re-export it (the jmap-filenode-server pattern). Remove the four CAPABILITY_* constants.

Affected: jmap-tasks-server, jmap-calendars-server, jmap-contacts-server, jmap-sharing-server.
title: P2: capability URI constants follow two competing conventions
